name: 2130 Prairie Avenue — the Murdoch house, rock-faced stone under a side-gabled front roof with a round corner tower, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Pictured: 2 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); both photographs of 2140 next door show it, and both are later than its building (the register's Murdoch house of about 1890). No building date or loss date is read for it here (T-3729).

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body at its south wall: column 620.5, row 1518.5 of sheet 35 at full size (T-3729), about 8.9 m behind and 1.2 m south of the draft's corner (the draft's fit had read a 9.75 m deep, 7 m wide stone block and set the rest of the outline as ranges and a bay), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading. Rotation -0.679 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, as the draft had it.
placement.symbolic_location: 2130 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2130 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body: 21.93 m from the rear wall (column 620.5) to the front (column 738.5, the outer edge of the blue band), and 9.85 m along the front from the south wall (row 1518.5) to the north wall (row 1465.5), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3729) and carried into this frame through the committed fit of the trace (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json, 0.1858 m a pixel). The sheet colours the block blue (stone) at the front and pink (brick) at the rear, divided on a diagonal: the stone front and brick rear the register reads. Its north wall steps in about 0.9 m (row 1470.5) over the rear 11.8 m (from column 684): not built, the body is one rectangle (L-k01-2130-murdoch-3729). The draft's fit had read only the largest stone rectangle (9.75 by 7 m) and set the rest as ranges and a bay.

stories.note: '2½B' printed on the 1911 sheet over the main block: two full storeys and a half storey in the roof, the side-gabled front roof's attic in both photographs. The round tower is '3B' (see bays).

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the block stone at the front and brick at the rear (the register's 'stone front and brick rear'); both photographs show the front and the tower in rough, rock-faced ashlar.

principal_floor_m.note: The principal floor about 1.4 m over the yard: the tower's ground-storey lights stand about a storey's sill over the fence's curb in the first photograph, and the porch's floor about the same; kept at the draft's figure, which the pictures do not contradict. T-3730 solves the cameras that measure it.

storey_heights_m.note: Two storeys of about 3.9 and 3.5 m: in the first photograph the tower's moulded string course between its first and second storeys and the one under its third (the main eave's level) divide the drum about 3.5 : 2.5 over the ground storey's lights and the second storey's; storey heights in the avenue's usual range for a house of about 1890. The camera ticket (T-3730) holds them to the pictures.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A rock-faced ashlar front on brick backing: a starting thickness from the contract's masonry range; no source measures it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A 13 in brick side wall, the contract's ordinary masonry thickness; no source measures it.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing before the door, its depth unread: the photograph sees the flight end-on from the north.

eave_overhang_m.note: The front's slate runs a little past the wall over its moulded course in the first photograph (the eave over the front's south bay, x 1575-1665 px, y 870-900 px); 0.3 m, its depth unread.

service_wall_brick.note: The side and rear walls the sheet colours brick, in the avenue's common brick behind a stone front: no picture shows them closely.

stone_front.note: Rough, rock-faced coursed ashlar over the whole front and the tower in both photographs (the register's 'stone front'), with smooth dressed sills, lintels and string courses. Pale in the Glessner/Van Osdel print and mid-grey in the Chicagology photograph: built in the avenue's Lemont limestone, its stone unread (no source names it). T-3730: the south flank is laid in the same rock-faced stone, whole length (stone_front.flanks). The Chicagology print, on its solved camera, shows the south wall's front part in the front's rock-faced coursed ashlar wherever 2140 does not hide it (from the corner about 3 m back, its second-storey light at x 1490-1530 px), where T-3729 had laid K03 brick; and sheet 35 colours the whole south edge of the main body blue: its diagonal between the blue and the pink runs from the south wall's rear corner (column 622, row 1518) to the north wall at about column 684, so the south flank is stone to the rear and only the north flank turns brick part-way back. The north flank stays K03 brick here: K01's flanks take one stopping length for both walls, the north one is seen in neither picture, and the sheet's stone on its front 10.1 m is recorded in L-k01-2130-murdoch-3729.

street_front_trim.note: Plain dressed stone lintels over the front's lights: both photographs show the lights cut square into the rough coursing with smooth heads and sills.

wall_head.note: No bracketed cornice on the front: the side-gabled roof's slope rises off the wall's moulded course, and the tower carries its own moulded course at its cone's eave (see bays).

roof_form.note: A side-gabled front block (T-3730): neither photograph, on its solved camera, shows a gable on the street front. The Chicagology print shows the south flank carried up as a gable in the front's rock-faced stone, its front rake falling from behind 2140's mansard to the front's south eave (x 1482-1590 px, y 740-877 px), and a slated ridge with cresting running along the avenue from it toward the tower (y 670 px at x 1465, 705 px at x 1550), the street slope falling from it to the front's eave; the Van Osdel print shows the same slope behind the tower. K01's gable roof (T-2459) is that roof: a ridge parallel to the front, the side walls carried up as coped gables. Behind the ridge nothing is seen (2140 hides the flank past its first few metres), so the rear slope is the kit's plain fall to the rear wall's head (L-k01-2130-murdoch-3730). Until T-3730 the front was carried up as a steep street gable over a hip (T-3729's reading), which neither picture shows.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The street slope's pitch, off the Chicagology print's south gable on its solved camera (T-3730): the rake from the front's south eave (8.8 m, x 1585 px, y 876 px) passes x 1482 px, y 740 px, which a 52 degree slope does (50 puts it 10 px low, 55 about 25 px high); with the ridge's line (y 670 px at x 1465, 705 px at x 1550) it sets the ridge about 4.0 m behind the front at about 13.9 m. Inside K05's steep band (45-65); the Van Osdel print shows the same steep slope behind the tower.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the main roof and the tower's cone in both photographs.

stoop_width_m.note: The porch's steps are hidden behind the fence in both pictures; the contract's ordinary flight.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the front's south end, inside the columned porch both photographs show south of the tower (the first photograph, x 1450-1660 px, y 1090-1200 px).

front_bays.note: Two bays along the front from its south corner: the door with a light over it in the flat stretch the sheet leaves south of the tower's bow (row 1500.5 to the south wall, 3.35 m), and the tower's (see bays).

side_bays.note: The south flank faces a 2.9 m side yard toward 2140 (the sheet) and is hidden behind 2140 in both pictures: four lights a storey at the kit's spacing.

north_bays.note: The north wall stands 0.56 m off the line with 2126 (the sheet, rows 1463 and 1465.5): a blind wall, as the avenue's walls on so narrow a gap.

rear_bays.note: No source sees the rear wall; a light a storey either side of the rear range.

sash_by_storey.note: The side and rear lights: no picture shows them; the kit's ordinary sash, the upper storey's kept clear of the steep eave's soffit.

basement_lights.note: The basement's area lights under the front's lights: the fence and its curb hide the plinth in both pictures; the kit's ordinary area light.

window_kit.note: Two-over-two sash in the front's and the tower's lights in both photographs.

entrance_kit.note: The door itself is in the porch's shadow in both pictures: the kit's panelled door on its stoop, square-headed (no arch shows over the porch's lintel).

windows.why_not_ordinary: the tower's ground-storey lights in both photographs (the first's x 1745-1790 and 1830-1845 px, y 1105-1190 px), round the drum
the tower's second-storey lights in both photographs (the first's x 1740-1790 and 1830-1845 px, y 940-1030 px)
the tower's short top stage over the main eave, its lights in both photographs (the first's x 1740-1790 and 1830-1850 px, y 810-880 px)

bays.note: The round tower the sheet draws at the front's north corner ('3B' in a circle, its stone bowed out over the front from row 1500.5 to the north wall, about 2.2 m proud at column 750) and both photographs show: a drum of rough ashlar in three stages, two storeys of tall lights and a short top stage of smaller ones over the main eave, under a slated cone on a moulded course with a finial. The sheet's dashed circle (columns 720-749.5) reads a drum about 2.8 m in radius on a centre about 0.6 m inside the front's face; K01 stands a single-capped front tower's centre on the face or before it, so it is built 2.4 m in radius on a centre 0.1 m before the face, 6.6 m along it: it bows 2.5 m proud (the sheet's 2.2 m) on a 4.8 m chord (the sheet's about 6.3 m), narrower along the front (L-k01-2130-murdoch-3729); its cone at 1.6 rise to 1 run (T-3730: T-3729 built it at 2.0, the print's 'height about its base's width'; on both pictures' solved cameras that cone's apex stood about 1.1 m over the pictures' — 60 px over the apex the Chicagology print's cone edges converge on behind the lamp head, 13 px over the Van Osdel print's at about 13 px a metre — and 1.6 brings both within about 0.2 m). Three lights a stage, evenly round the drum's face: the pictures see two or three of each, and T-3730's cameras place them.

chimneys.note: The Chicagology print shows one short, broad brick stack just south of the tower's cone (x 1598-1645 px, its top at about y 675 px): on the solved camera it stands on the ridge (u 17.93, 4.0 m behind the front) about 9.0 m from the south wall, about 1.0 m along the ridge (the print's breadth, about 47 px), its top the kit's 0.75 m over the ridge (T-3730); it had stood at u 13.0, far behind, where the hip's ridge ran. The second, near the rear on the south wall, is reconstructed.

rainwater.note: No gutter or pipe reads in either picture. T-3730: with the front block side-gabled, the house carries none: a K01 gable roof hangs no eave gutter yet (T-2459) and neither picture shows a pipe on the front for front_pipes to stand; until T-3730 the kit's half-round copper gutter ran round the hip's eaves with two pipes down the south flank, which no picture saw either.

boundary.note: An iron railing on a stone curb along the street line, with stone piers, in the first photograph (x 1440-1840 px, y 1180-1290 px, a capped pier at x 1755-1795 px): the kit's spear railing on its curb and a walk gate on piers; the railing's pattern and the piers' caps are not read (L-k01-2130-murdoch-3729). The railing stands 0.25 m inside the sheet's street line (column 770), clear of the walk; the lot lines are the sheet's (rows 1534 and 1463).

yard.note: The walk to the stoop in stone flags, as the avenue's other K01 fronts.

rear_wings.note: The '1B' brick range the 1911 sheet draws behind the main block: columns 572-620.5 and rows 1481-1508, so 9.0 m deep and 5.0 m wide, its rear corners chamfered (built square). One storey under a flat roof; no picture sees it.

gable_roof.note: The ridge 4.0 m behind the front's plane, at about 13.9 m (the Chicagology print's rake and ridge on its solved camera, see roof_pitch_deg), so the rear slope falls about 16 degrees to the rear wall's head, the kit's plain gable; no picture sees it (L-k01-2130-murdoch-3730). Both side walls are carried up as K05 coped parapets: the south one, the print's stone gable over the front part, in the flank's rock-faced stone (stone_front.flanks); the north one, which neither picture sees, to match in the north wall's brick. The print shows a plain verge on the rake; the coping is the kit's.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½ and 3B dwelling (D), stone front and brick rear divided on the diagonal, with a round bay on its Prairie front'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: T-3729 (piece 1 of T-1927, the S16 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2351) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K03 brick body behind a rock-faced stone front, a K08 round tower of three stages under a slated cone, the front carried up as a steep street gable, K06 sash, a K07 door, the K11 railing and the one-storey brick rear range — instead of the draft builder. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (the outline, the '3B' tower's bow, '2½B', the stone/brick division and the '1B' range), and the two photographs of 2140 next door, which show this house past 2140's north side (forms only). What is not built, and why, is the liberty L-k01-2130-murdoch-3729; T-3730 solves the photographs' cameras and works the match down. T-3730, second pass: the front is roofed as the side-gabled block both pictures show (K01's gable roof, its ridge 4.0 m behind the front at about 13.9 m, the south gable in the flank's stone) in place of T-3729's street gable over a hip, and the print's stack stands on that ridge.
called: 2130 Prairie Avenue — the Murdoch house, rock-faced stone under a side-gabled front roof with a round corner tower
